clues.text: This city is the capital of Normandy in north west France. It sits on the River Seine, north west of Paris.
clues.narrowing: The capital of Normandy, on the Seine.

source.quote: Rouen is the capital of Normandy in northwestern France, situated on the River Seine northwest of Paris.

clues.text: Rain falls all year in this port. The mild air comes from the sea, and no month is dry.
clues.narrowing: Mild sea air and rain in all months.

source.quote: Rouen has a temperate oceanic climate with mild temperatures and precipitation throughout the year.

clues.text: A young girl was tried and burned at the stake here in 1431. Her name was Joan of Arc.
clues.narrowing: Where Joan of Arc was burned in 1431.

source.quote: Joan of Arc was tried and burned at the stake in Rouen in 1431.

clues.text: A huge clock from the year 1389 still ticks in this town. It hangs over a street in the old town.
clues.narrowing: A great clock from 1389 over a street.

source.quote: the Gros-Horloge, an astronomical clock dating from 1389

clues.text: Monet came here to paint the great west front of the church. He made more than thirty views of it in sun and mist.
clues.narrowing: The church front Monet painted thirty times.

source.quote: Claude Monet painted the façade of Rouen Cathedral in a famous series of over thirty paintings.

clues.text: This city sits on the Ohio River in the south west of Indiana. It is the third most populous city in the state.
clues.narrowing: A river city in the south west of Indiana.

source.quote: Evansville is a city in Vanderburgh County, Indiana, United States, situated on the Ohio River in the southwestern part of the state. It is the third-most populous city in Indiana.

clues.text: The air here is hot and wet in the long hot months. Winters are much cooler, and storms can hit in spring.
clues.narrowing: Hot wet summers and much cooler winters.

source.quote: Evansville has a humid subtropical climate, with hot, humid summers, cooler winters, and occasional severe weather in spring and fall.

clues.text: Hugh McGary Jr. set up this town in the year 1812. He bought about 441 acres of land for it.
clues.narrowing: Founded by Hugh McGary Jr. in 1812.

source.quote: Evansville was founded in 1812 by Hugh McGary Jr., who purchased approximately 441 acres.

clues.text: A huge LST ship from the war is tied up here. Men give tours and tell how it hit the beach on D-Day.
clues.narrowing: A war era LST ship you can tour.

source.quote: The USS LST-325, a World War II landing ship, is moored in Evansville as a museum ship.

clues.text: This town is the home of the Otters ball team. They play at Bosse Field, one of the first big parks in the land.
clues.narrowing: Home of the Otters, at Bosse Field.

source.quote: Bosse Field, one of the oldest ballparks in the United States, is home to the Evansville Otters.

clues.text: This town in south Germany sits on the east bank of the Danube. An old town in the next state lies just over the river.
clues.narrowing: A Danube town in Bavaria, by the river bank.

source.quote: Neu-Ulm is a town in Bavaria, Germany, located on the eastern bank of the Danube River, adjacent to Ulm in Baden-Württemberg.

clues.text: This town is one of the places with the most fog days in the land. The river mist hangs low in the fall.
clues.narrowing: One of the most fog prone towns in Germany.

source.quote: Neu-Ulm is among the places with the most fog days in Germany.

clues.text: This town got its name in the year 1814. At that time, the land on the east bank went to the King of Bavaria.
clues.narrowing: Named in 1814, when the bank went to Bavaria.

source.quote: Neu-Ulm received its name in 1814 when the eastern bank area came under the Kingdom of Bavaria.

clues.text: A tower of bricks from the war days still stands here. The Edwin Scharff Museum sits at its base, full of art.
clues.narrowing: An old war tower with an art museum.

source.quote: The Edwin Scharff Museum is located near a historic tower in Neu-Ulm.

clues.text: Men from this town row in the big boat races on the Danube. A top rowing club trains on the river each week.
clues.narrowing: A town known for its rowing club.

source.quote: Neu-Ulm is known for its rowing club on the Danube.

clues.text: This city sits on a flat plain south of the big port of Casablanca. It is a town in the north part of Morocco.
clues.narrowing: A plain city south of Casablanca.

source.quote: Settat is a city in Morocco located on the Chaouia plain south of Casablanca.

clues.text: Hot, dry days fill the warm months here. The rains come in the cool months, from late fall to early spring.
clues.narrowing: Dry heat, then rain in the cool season.

source.quote: Settat has a hot semi-arid climate. The average temperature in Settat is 18.75 °C (65.8 °F)

clues.text: A fort was built here in the late 1700s. It was part of a chain of strong points in the time of Sultan Mohammed ben Abdallah.
clues.narrowing: A fort built in the late 1700s.

source.quote: Settat was developed as a kasbah/fortification in the 18th century under Sultan Mohammed ben Abdallah.

clues.text: Each year, men ride here for a big horse fair. They show off fast Arabian horses and old horse skills.
clues.narrowing: A horse fair with Arabian horses.

source.quote: Settat is known for an annual horse festival celebrating Arabian horses and equestrian traditions.

clues.text: This town has the main campus of Hassan First University. Young men and women come from all over the land to study.
clues.narrowing: Home of Hassan First University.

source.quote: Settat is home to Hassan First University.

clues.text: This city is the capital of Koshi Province in the east of Nepal. It is a big hub for trade near the line with India.
clues.narrowing: The capital of Koshi Province, in east Nepal.

source.quote: Biratnagar is a metropolitan city in Nepal, the capital of Koshi Province, and an industrial and commercial hub in eastern Nepal.

clues.text: The big rains come from June to the fall. The days stay hot, and the air is wet for most of the year.
clues.narrowing: Hot days with monsoon rain from June.

source.quote: Biratnagar has a humid subtropical climate with a monsoon season from June to October; summers are hot and humid with heavy rainfall.

clues.text: The jute mills built here long ago made this town grow. It was one of the first mill towns in the land.
clues.narrowing: An old jute mill town of Nepal.

source.quote: Biratnagar developed as an industrial city with the establishment of jute mills in the early 20th century.

clues.text: Men still work the big jute mills here. The mills grind on and give work to folks all over the east.
clues.narrowing: Still known for its working jute mills.

source.quote: Biratnagar remains known for its jute industry.

clues.text: This is the main trade gate to India in the east. Trucks cross the line here all day with food and goods.
clues.narrowing: The main east gate for trade with India.

source.quote: Biratnagar serves as a major border trade point with India in eastern Nepal.

clues.text: This city in Maharashtra is on the west bank of the Sina River. It is one of the old towns of the Deccan.
clues.narrowing: A Deccan city on the Sina River.

source.quote: Ahmadnagar is a city in Maharashtra, India, located on the western bank of the Sina River.

clues.text: This town is hot and dry for most of the year. The rains are brief, and they do not fall each year in the same way.
clues.narrowing: Hot, dry, with brief and fickle rains.

source.quote: Ahmadnagar has a hot semi-arid climate, with hot and dry conditions for most of the year and a brief, variable monsoon.

clues.text: Malik Ahmad set up this town in the year 1490. He made his own state here and broke from the Bahmani rule.
clues.narrowing: Founded by Malik Ahmad in 1490.

source.quote: Ahmadnagar was founded in 1490 by Malik Ahmad Nizam Shah I, who established an independent sultanate.

clues.text: A queen named Chand Bibi held the fort here in 1599. She fought off the Mughal host with great skill.
clues.narrowing: Where Queen Chand Bibi held the fort.

source.quote: Chand Bibi defended Ahmadnagar Fort against Mughal forces in the 1590s.

clues.text: The tomb of the man who set up this town still stands here. Folks come to see the old tomb and fort.
clues.narrowing: The founder's tomb and the old fort.

source.quote: The tomb of Ahmad Nizam Shah is located in Ahmadnagar.

clues.text: This city is the capital of the West Pomeranian Voivodeship. It is a port on the Oder River in north west Poland.
clues.narrowing: A port and capital in north west Poland.

source.quote: Szczecin is the capital of the West Pomeranian Voivodeship in northwestern Poland, a major seaport on the Oder River.

clues.text: Sea air keeps this port mild all year. The winters are cool, the warm months are mild, and the rain is not heavy.
clues.narrowing: Mild sea air with cool winters.

source.quote: Szczecin has an oceanic climate with mild temperatures year-round, cool winters, and moderate rainfall.

clues.text: Ships from this port have sailed the Baltic for a long time. Hansa ships once tied up here to trade in grain and fish.
clues.narrowing: An old Hansa port on the Baltic.

source.quote: Szczecin was a member of the Hanseatic League, a historic trading association of Baltic ports.

clues.text: A round white hall here looks like a hat from the space age. Folks call it the flying saucer of the town.

source.quote: The Szczecin Philharmonic hall, with its distinctive white angular design, is a landmark of the city.

clues.text: This port is the home of a tall ship race stop. Big ships with tall masts fill the port in some years.
clues.narrowing: A stop for the tall ships races.

source.quote: Szczecin has hosted the Tall Ships Races on several occasions.
